name: if() chooses without working out the branch it did not take, and text is compared as a code
why: These two arrived together because neither is useful alone. A rate table is the case that broke the old rule: a contribution ceiling that differs by Bundesland, a rate that differs by number of children. Branching needs a conditional, and the thing branched on is a select, whose value is a stored code. The sharp part is laziness: `if(months == 0, 0, costs / months)` must answer zero, and an implementation that works out both arms gets the division's unknown instead — turning a guard into the very thing it guards against. The other sharp part is that a blank text field is the empty code, not unknown, so a record nobody has set a state on answers a definite false rather than spreading unknown through the whole table.

cases.why: The case the whole file exists for. A ceiling that differs by Bundesland was simply unwritable before: no conditional, and no way to compare a select to its code.

A blank select is the EMPTY code, exactly as a blank number is zero. So the test is definitely false and the else branch is taken — not unknown. An implementation answering null here has treated an unfilled field as an unworkable figure.
Codes are compared exactly. Case folding would quietly accept a value no option offers, hiding the authoring mistake rather than showing it.
Either quote delimits a literal. They are the same literal.

LAZINESS, and it is not an optimisation. Both arms worked out means the division by zero happens anyway, `costs / months` is unknown, and the answer comes back unknown — from an expression whose author explicitly guarded against exactly that. The guard would be worse than useless.
And the other way, so the case above is not passing because the else branch is broken.
A test nobody could work out makes the whole conditional unknown. Neither answer is chosen, because choosing either would be inventing which way it went.
Nested, which is how a table with more than two rows is written.
Boolean logic over several codes — the shape a west/east split actually takes.
An `if` answering TEXT rather than a number. The two answers agree on their kind, and that kind is the result.
A text answer can also be unknown, which is the only way a text ever is — every text FIELD reads as a code or as the blank.
Two text fields compared to each other, not to a literal.
!= is the negation of == once both sides are known, and both sides are always known when they are fields.
A conditional answering a boolean, so `if` is not a numeric function wearing three arguments.
The bound is still the better way to write a bound. min/max did not become redundant when the branch arrived.
